answer: Because the copper index resolves every citation against the oasis checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the river audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 291 aliases therefore burns the authoring cost 291 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 39 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
